# Exact two-sided scalar frontier at Brunn--Minkowski equality
to a residual-row shortcut. It is not a proof or counterexample of OC.
The empty-section classification below concerns CLOSED sections on both
sides of the cutting hyperplane; their common boundary has zero volume.

## 1. Definitions and theorem

Let d>=1, N>=2, theta_j>0 with sum theta_j=1, and let A_j be full-dimensional
compact convex bodies in R^d. Fix coordinates (t,y), with t in R and y in
R^(d-1), and the closed halfspaces H_+={t<=0}, H_-={t>=0}. Put

    a_j=|A_j|^(1/d)>0,
    p_j=|A_j intersect H_+|/|A_j| in [0,1],
    s=sum_j theta_j a_j,
    c=sum_j theta_j a_j p_j^(1/d),
    r=sum_j theta_j a_j (1-p_j)^(1/d).

Let K be a convex body containing sum_j theta_j A_j. We restrict this
local theorem to the exact whole-body BM equality slice

    |K|=s^d.                                                 (1)

Write u=|K intersect H_+|^(1/d), so the opposite root is
v=(s^d-u^d)^(1/d). The following classification is sharp for prescribed
positive a_j, weights theta_j, fractions p_j, and prescribed statuses
of every zero-volume endpoint section.

A zero-volume closed section may be TANGENT (nonempty) or EMPTY. A proper
cut (0<p_j<1) has both closed sections nonempty. A p_j=0 section has a
positive-volume H_- part and either a tangent or empty H_+ part; p_j=1
has the symmetric possibilities. Define E_+ to mean at least one closed
H_+ endpoint section is empty, and E_- symmetrically. Set

    U=(s^d-r^d)^(1/d).

Then the possible source cap roots u are exactly:

* Neither E_+ nor E_-: the closed interval [c,U].
* E_+ and not E_-: [0,U) if at least one p_j>0; the singleton {0}
  if every p_j=0.
* E_- and not E_+: (c,s] if at least one p_j<1; the singleton {s}
  if every p_j=1.
* Both E_+ and E_-: the closed interval [0,s].

Every value in these sets is attained by HOMOTHETIC translated endpoint
bodies, with K exactly their weighted Minkowski sum. Thus the body BM
comparison is exactly tight throughout. The first interval is nonempty:
the triangle inequality in R^2 for the l_d norm gives

    (c^d+r^d)^(1/d)
      <=sum_j theta_j [(a_j p_j^(1/d))^d
                       +(a_j(1-p_j)^(1/d))^d]^(1/d)=s.       (2)

For d=1, equality holds in (2), and the first interval is a singleton.
No assertion is made that these scalar realizations preserve a specified
larger lattice family, a KKT system, or global criticality. Section5 gives
a separate actual globally critical lattice example.

## 2. Necessary inequalities, with the empty/tangent distinction retained

Whenever every A_j intersect H_+ is nonempty, convexity gives

    sum_j theta_j (A_j intersect H_+) subset K intersect H_+.

Ordinary BM, valid also for nonempty lower-dimensional compact convex
sets, gives u>=c. Zero volume is not an empty-set convention here: a
nonempty tangent face really is a usable Minkowski summand. Similarly,
if every A_j intersect H_- is nonempty, then v>=r, hence u<=U.

This proves necessity when neither side has an empty section, and gives
the non-strict bound on the other side when exactly one side has an
empty section. The strict endpoint exclusion follows from a geometric
strip, not from an assertion that zero volume is positive volume.

Suppose E_+ holds and E_- does not, with some p_j>0. An endpoint A_i
whose H_+ section is empty is compact and has min_{x in A_i} t(x)=delta>0.
All closed H_- sections are nonempty, and

    L=sum_j theta_j (A_j intersect H_-)

is full dimensional: it contains a translate of theta_i A_i, after
choosing one point in each other nonempty summand. Every point of L has
t>=theta_i delta>0. BM gives |L|>=r^d. If u=U, then u>0 because at least
one p_j>0, and v=r>0 because endpoint i is wholly in H_-. The convex body
K consequently has interior points on both sides of t=0. A segment
between two such interior points crosses t=0 inside int K, so there is
an open ball about some point of K at t=0. Its portion

    0<t<theta_i delta

has positive volume, lies in K intersect H_-, and is disjoint from L.
This contradicts |K intersect H_-|=r^d>=|L|. Thus u<U. If all p_j=0,
then r=s and u=0 follows from v>=r. The case E_- but not E_+ is obtained
by replacing t with -t. If both types of empty section occur, only the
trivial bounds 0<=u<=s remain; Section4 realizes every value.

The same strip proof in fact makes the side-BM inequality strict for
any proper target cut whenever an opposite endpoint has a positive
support gap. It does not require (1); equation(1) converts it into the
excluded scalar endpoint described above.

## 3. Homothetic frusta realize the full tangent/proper interval

First suppose d>=2. Choose a (d-1)-dimensional convex body E containing
0 and of volume one. For tau in [0,1] let

    h_tau(t)=(1-tau)t+tau(1-t),       0<=t<=1,
    J_tau=int_0^1 h_tau(t)^(d-1) dt>0,
    D_tau={(t,y):0<=t<=1,
                    y in J_tau^(-1/(d-1)) h_tau(t) E}.

Because h_tau is affine and nonnegative, D_tau is a compact convex
body. Cavalieri gives |D_tau|=1. Its prefix-volume function is

    F_tau(q)=J_tau^(-1) int_0^q h_tau(t)^(d-1) dt,
                     0<=q<=1.                             (3)

It is continuous and strictly increasing from 0 to1; strict increase
holds because h_tau>0 on (0,1). The map (tau,q)->F_tau(q) is continuous.
For each prescribed p_j in [0,1], the unique quantile
q_j(tau)=F_tau^(-1)(p_j) is therefore continuous in tau. For example,
any convergent subsequence of quantiles along tau_m->tau has a limit
q, equation(3) gives F_tau(q)=p_j, and uniqueness identifies q. The
endpoints p_j=0,1 simply give q_j=0,1.

Define actual bodies and their common fixed cutting halfspace by

    A_j(tau)=a_j [D_tau-q_j(tau)e_t],
    K(tau)=sum_j theta_j A_j(tau)
           =s[D_tau-q_0(tau)e_t],
    q_0(tau)=s^(-1) sum_j theta_j a_j q_j(tau),
    H_+={t<=0}.                                             (4)

The equality in (4) is the elementary identity
sum b_j D=(sum b_j)D for positive b_j and convex D. Thus these are
homothetic translated copies, the FULL target body has volume s^d,
and one and the same halfspace gives the specified endpoint fractions.
Every zero-volume endpoint section is tangent because q_j is0 or1,
and D_tau meets both endpoint hyperplanes t=0,1. The target root

    u(tau)=s F_tau(q_0(tau))^(1/d)                           (5)

is continuous. At tau=0, F_0(q)=q^d, so u(0)=c. At tau=1,
F_1(q)=1-(1-q)^d, so v(1)=r and u(1)=U. The intermediate value theorem
therefore attains every number between c and U. The side-BM
inequalities from Section2 show that no value outside that interval
occurs. No monotonicity in tau is needed or asserted.

For d=1 take D=[0,1], with F(q)=q. Equations(4) apply unchanged and give
u=c=U. This proves the first case in all dimensions, including nonempty
tangent endpoint sections.

## 4. Strict support gaps realize the other intervals

All constructions in this section continue using equations(4), except
that zero/one quantiles may be moved outside [0,1]. The endpoint
fractions then remain exactly zero/one, while the corresponding closed
section becomes genuinely empty. Extend F_tau by0 to q<=0 and by1 to
q>=1; this extension is continuous.

Suppose E_+ holds and E_- does not. Use the tau=1 frustum, whose tangent
baseline target root is U. For every prescribed empty H_+ section
necessarily p_j=0; replace its q_j=0 by q_j=-delta, using the same
parameter delta>0. Leave all other quantiles unchanged. These endpoint
bodies have strictly positive minimum t=a_j delta, so their H_+
sections really are empty. All prescribed tangent statuses remain
unchanged, and all H_- sections remain nonempty. The target q_0 decreases
linearly with delta with a strictly positive rate. Consequently its
root u decreases continuously from the limiting value U at delta=0 to
0, which it reaches for all sufficiently large delta. If U>0, every
u in [0,U) is attained with delta>0. If U=0, all p_j=0 and the root is
identically0. For d=1 the same argument uses the interval D.

For E_- and not E_+, use the tau=0 frustum and replace q_j=1 by
q_j=1+delta exactly at prescribed empty H_- sections. The baseline root
is c, and increasing delta makes the target root range through (c,s],
with the all-p_j=1 case giving the singleton {s}.

If both E_+ and E_- occur, fix any one frustum, keep all proper and
tangent quantiles fixed, set q_j=-alpha at prescribed empty H_+
sections and q_j=1+beta at prescribed empty H_- sections, where
alpha,beta>0. In the target weighted average q_0, alpha has a strictly
negative coefficient and beta a strictly positive coefficient. Their
positive ranges let q_0 take every real value: for any desired value,
one may first choose alpha sufficiently large and then solve for a
positive beta. Thus the extended target prefix F(q_0) takes every value
in [0,1], proving the last case. Every construction retains exact
whole-body BM equality.

For two bodies with theta_1=theta_2=1/2, this is an ACTUAL midpoint
convex-body construction: take

    C=conv(({ -1 } times A_1) union ({ 1 } times A_2)).

Its integer base is exactly {-1,0,1}; its three actual sections are
A_1, K=(A_1+A_2)/2, A_2; it is full dimensional in R times R^d; and the
single ambient halfspace H_+={t<=0} has exactly the traces used above.
Thus the local theorem never silently replaces a midpoint section by
a nonrealizable abstract volume array.

More generally, prescribed rational weights theta_j=m_j/(sum_i m_i)
can be realized at an integer source0 using the affinely independent
integer bases z_j=m_N e_j (j<N) and z_N=-sum_{j<N}m_j e_j. Their
barycentric combination at0 has exactly the specified weights, and
at that base the lifted convex hull has section sum theta_j A_j.
There can be additional integer fibers, whose volumes and depths are
not controlled or ignored by a claim here.

## 5. A globally critical Minkowski-affine interval obstruction

The following n=d=1 example strengthens the earlier critical interval
row obstruction: WHOLE-FIBER midpoint BM is tight, while the unchanged
residual-row inequality still fails. Let the actual centered fibers be

    A_-1=[-1/2,1/2], A_0=[-3/4,3/4], A_1=[-1,1].          (6)

Their half-width is the affine function 3/4+z/4 on [-1,1]. Hence

    C={(z,x):-1<=z<=1, |x|<=3/4+z/4}

is a full-dimensional convex body, its integer fibers are exactly(6),
and A_0=(A_-1+A_1)/2. Their lengths are(1,3/2,2), their total is M=9/2,
and max V=2<9/4=M/2. Thus every fiber is strictly nonheavy.

At (0,0), normalize any through-point halfspace with nonzero continuous
coefficient, after reflecting x if necessary, to x+a z>=0. Its middle
contribution is3/4. Let T_R(t)=|[-R,R] intersect [t,infinity)|. Its endpoint
contribution is

    T_(1/2)(a)+T_1(-a)
       =2-[T_1(a)-T_(1/2)(a)] >=1.                        (7)

The difference in brackets is the captured length in the set difference
[-1,1] minus [-1/2,1/2], whose total length is1. A purely integer
through-point CLOSED halfspace contains the entire middle fiber and at
least one endpoint, so has mass at least5/2. Boundary fiber mass is
therefore retained. Every containing halfspace can be moved inward to
pass through the point, and (7) gives raw depth at least7/4.

For L>=1 the halfspaces

    H_+(L)={x-Lz>=0}, H_-(L)={-x-Lz>=0}

have exact mass7/4: the left fiber is fully captured, the middle is cut
in half, and the right contributes zero length. They cover the middle
fiber. At any other (0,x), choosing the sign toward its shorter middle
side and a sufficiently large L gives mass7/4-|x|. At the extreme bases,
arbitrarily large integer tilts isolate an own-fiber half interval, and
own-fiber contributions give their maximum depths exactly1/2 and1.
Thus (0,0) is the UNIQUE globally deepest mixed point and

    Q=7/4,             Q/M=7/18>1/4.                     (8)

Equation(7) also classifies the entire critical menu at (0,0). Equality
requires both outside pieces of [-1,1] minus [-1/2,1/2] to be captured;
with the positive continuous normalization this means a<=-1. Reflecting
x gives the other sign. Pure integer caps are not critical. A cap containing the center strictly,
with nonzero continuous normal, has strictly more middle-fiber mass than
its parallel translate through the center, and the other fiber masses
cannot decrease; it consequently has mass greater than Q. Hence every
critical cap is H_+(L) or H_-(L) with L>=1 and has the SAME residual-length
array (0,3/4,2), including tangent cases L=1.

For an exact original cap cover use H_+(2),H_-(2) and the two isolated
right midpoint caps

    G_+={x+4(z-1)>=0}, G_-={-x+4(z-1)>=0}.

The H pair covers bases -1 and0, and the G pair covers the right fiber;
the latter caps exclude the other two fibers and each has mass1<Q.
The residual obstacles are exactly

    e=(0,3/4,1).

The d=1 convex-majorant program minimizes h_-+h_0+h_+ subject to h>=e
and h_-+h_+>=2h_0. Its optimum is9/4, attained at the affine vector
h=(1/2,3/4,1). At EVERY optimum, h_0=3/4 and h_-+h_+=3/2. Since the
endpoint obstacles sum to1<3/2, at least one endpoint multiplier vanishes.
In any nonnegative barycentric KKT flow, the extreme bases have no
outgoing flow; the only possible nonzero row satisfies

    mu_(0,-1)=mu_(0,1)=t.

Objective derivatives are all1. Endpoint stationarity gives
lambda_-=lambda_+=1-t. One zero multiplier therefore forces t=1,
lambda_-=lambda_+=0, lambda_0=3. These values are valid KKT data, since
the displayed affine optimum makes the active support inequalities tight
and the center obstacle is active. Every primal/KKT choice for this
specified program yields the same terminal row, uniform on {-1,0,1}.
For EVERY globally critical cap its ORIGINAL residual roots consequently
satisfy

    sum_j theta_j f(j)=(0+3/4+2)/3=11/12>3/4=f(0),
    row gap=1/6.                                          (9)

The full-body root comparison in precisely this row is tight:

    (1+3/2+2)/3=3/2=|A_0|.

The own-fiber cap fraction at the active source is exactly gamma_1=1/2.
Thus there is neither total-body BM slack nor own-centroid cap surplus
to pay the positive gap(9). Genuine global criticality, complete integer
fibers, strict nonheaviness, and all-KKT/all-critical-cap optimization do
not change this conclusion for the specified cover and program.
This example is strictly ABOVE OC, as equation(8) states.

## 6. The simplex equality-slice obstruction and scope of scalar corrections

Let gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d and kappa_d=(1-gamma_d)^(1/d), d>=1. Prescribe
endpoint volume roots a,b>0, left fraction1 with its opposite closed
section empty, and right fraction0 with its captured closed section
empty. Section4 realizes every source cap fraction eta in [0,1] with
K=(A+B)/2 and |K|=((a+b)/2)^d. In particular take a simplex for the
common homothetic body and arrange the target cutting plane through
its centroid in a canonical simplex direction. Then eta=gamma_d,
whole-body BM is tight, and the own canonical cap has no excess over
gamma_d. The midpoint residual-root comparison nevertheless has gap

    b/2-kappa_d(a+b)/2,

which is positive exactly when b/(a+b)>kappa_d. To see directly that
these prescribed statuses and target threshold coexist for a simplex,
use any height coordinate in which the canonical centroid plane has
quantile q_* in (0,1). Choose endpoint quantiles q_A>1 and q_B<0 so that
(a q_A+b q_B)/(a+b)=q_*; choosing q_A sufficiently large determines a
strictly negative q_B. The endpoint bodies are a(T-q_A e) and
b(T-q_B e), while K is their exact homothetic midpoint.

As a tends to0 with b=1, this gap tends to(1-kappa_d)/2>0 although the
fully captured endpoint volume a^d tends to0. Thus no universal local
correction depending only on that fully captured volume and tending
to0 with it can bound the residual-root loss, even after imposing exact
whole-body BM and a canonical source-centroid cut. The source cap mass
or additional genuinely global data cannot be omitted. No global
criticality is asserted for this arbitrary-dimension limiting family;
Section5 supplies the separate fully verified critical example in d=1.

The sharp scalar frontier is therefore both a positive local theorem
and a limit on this route. It does not supply a parity charge, choose
an OC center, or control a general mixed-integer halfspace depth.
